assessment:
The table watches you cast a tutor and assumes you just found the kill. Let them assume it. Most wishes here buy the engine, and the engine looks like value right up until it is lethal.

Start with what arrives without any help, because it is nearly everything. By turn ten you are holding a drain 82.3% of the time, renewable fodder 82.3%, a free sacrifice outlet 78.5% and an ignition source 73.8% — so never spend a wish on a covered class. Those cards are already coming.

One class is not covered. Fast mana is three cards and 43.6% of games, the smallest and lowest-rated engine class on the sheet — the single non-kill errand a wish is allowed to run, and every entry below that runs it says so out loud.

Now the heart of the matter. The primary line — Yawgmoth from the zone, Nest of Scarabs, a drain, roughly two drains per body on board (stacks 002, 003 and 004) — is assembled by turn six in 7.5% of games on your own draws. A wish takes it to 38.9%. Nest is one card in ninety-nine, and these five tutors are the only redundancy it has, so Nest of Scarabs is the default fetch. Demand a reason to deviate.

Six kill shapes, every one signed by the checker. Learn them by name so you can say which one you are a card away from. KILL E is the Nest engine above. KILL C is Exquisite Blood plus any gain-and-drain body — the earliest assembler at a mean of turn 5.1 and the biggest mover on the sheet, 6.6% to 42.6% with a wish, and stack 012 says the loop is mandatory, not a draw. KILL A (stack 009) and KILL B (stack 011) are the Gravecrawler loops, unbounded, 18.2% and 12.0% assisted. KILL D (stack 010) and KILL F (stack 014) are the undying lines — lethal but library-bounded, because your commander's draw is mandatory. Stack 014 prices F at thirty activations against roughly twenty-five cards of margin, so count before you start, never during.

Two cards carry the loop kills, so let arithmetic pick the fetch. Gravecrawler turns up on your own draws 17.0% of the time by turn ten and completes both unbounded kills; Bastion of Remembrance at 17.8% is the payoff half of three signed lines. A wish on either is a wish on several kills at once.

Name the shape, then check its precondition. KILL A and KILL B cast Gravecrawler out of the graveyard, which needs a Zombie the loop never sacrifices — Warren Soultrader in 009, Carrion Feeder in 011. Fetch Gravecrawler with no second Zombie and you have bought a 2/1 that cannot block.

One wish is the emergency brake. Feed the Swarm is the only card in the ninety-nine that answers a noncreature permanent — 17.1% on your own draws, 67.1% when a wish buys it. When an enchantment locks your graveyard, that is the fetch, at any price.

Two limits. You draw a tutor at all in 61.2% of games by turn ten, so build every plan to work without one and treat the wish as the upgrade, not the plan. And there is no union kill rate anywhere on the sheet — each shape is priced alone. Quote the numbers separately and never add them.

targets.scenario: Turn three, end step of the player before you, {B} open. Yawgmoth is the turn-four play — he lands there in 7,188 of 10,000 games — and no engine piece is on your battlefield.
targets.why: The default fetch, and the whole reason this deck runs five tutors. The primary line is together by turn six in 7.5% of games on your own draws and 38.9% with a wish — Nest is the one-of every version of that engine routes through, so the wish IS the consistency. Two life at instant speed, the draw step delivers it, three mana casts it, and the commander walks into a running engine: stacks 002, 003 and 004 signed the shape at roughly two drains per body per activation.

citations.quote: stack the classes you want every game (ramp, draw, removal, enablers), tutor only the irreplaceable

targets.scenario: Player 2 resolves Rest in Peace with your Gravecrawler already in the graveyard. Your board is a sacrifice outlet and two bodies, and it is Player 2's end step with {B} open.
targets.why: Stop the bleeding, because a graveyard lock is not an inconvenience here — two signed kills cast Gravecrawler out of the graveyard, so that enchantment deletes them both. Feed the Swarm is the only card among all eighty entries that answers a noncreature permanent: 17.1% on your own draws by turn ten, 67.1% when a wish buys it, which makes this wish most of your outs. Book it at their end step, cast it on your turn, pay the life without flinching.

citations.quote: ends the game or ends my deck's function

targets.scenario: End step of the player before you, turn seven. Warren Soultrader and Bastion of Remembrance are both on the battlefield, you have {B} untapped, and the table is spent — Player 2 tapped out for a six-drop, Player 4 down to two cards.
targets.why: Take the cheapest complete kill on the board: one black at instant speed and two life. Draw it, cast it for {B}, and stack 009 runs — each sacrifice to Soultrader mints the Treasure that pays the next cast, your life stays net zero, and every seat goes down together. Soultrader is the Zombie that switches Gravecrawler on and the loop never touches him, because his cost reads sacrifice ANOTHER creature. Count the table's open mana before you start.

citations.quote: assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing

targets.scenario: Turn one. One Swamp, {B} open, a second land in hand and no acceleration anywhere. Nobody has committed anything and nobody is watching you.
targets.why: This wish exists on turn one and nowhere else, so take it while it is live. Ritual arrives on your turn-two draw: Swamp plus Ritual is three black, the second land is the fourth mana, and that is Yawgmoth on turn two — the sim records him there in 718 of 10,000 games. Fast mana is the one engine class the deck does not deliver on its own — three cards, 43.6% by turn ten — so acceleration is the one non-kill errand worth a wish. Own the judgment: the goldfish models no rituals, so this line sits above the sheet, not inside it.

citations.quote: coming out too slowly is an easy way to lose a game

tutors.notes: Two life is never free in this deck. You are already paying Yawgmoth one per activation, plus Bitterblossom, Necropotence, Black Market Connections, City of Brass, Ancient Tomb, Cabal Pit and Ifnir Deadlands — so fire this while your total is comfortable and stop treating the cost as rounding. And fire it as the instant it is: the end step before your own turn is almost always the moment, because the transit turn then costs you nothing.

targets.scenario: Turn five, five mana after your land drop. Marauding Blight-Priest is on the battlefield and nobody has pointed removal at it — the table is reading you as a value deck.
targets.why: Buy the biggest mover on the sheet. KILL C runs 6.6% on your own draws and 42.6% with a wish, assembling earliest at a mean of turn 5.1 — and Exquisite Blood is the half only a to-hand tutor delivers, because at mana value 5 a bargained Beseech can never free-cast it and a top-of-library wish costs you the turn you need for the cast. Demonic does not care what the card costs; this is the wish that fits. Stack 012 signed the shape: the loop is mandatory, emphatically not a draw, and it takes every opponent to zero at once.

citations.quote: stack the classes you want every game (ramp, draw, removal, enablers), tutor only the irreplaceable

targets.scenario: Turn eight, seven or more mana. Yawgmoth and Bastion of Remembrance are on the battlefield and you have two non-Human bodies you are happy to feed him — Viscera Seer and Gravecrawler, say.
targets.why: Reach for the card no other wish in this suite can reach — mana value 6 sits outside every cap you own. He turns your commander's own ability into KILL D: the -1/-1 counter annihilates undying's +1/+1 at the next check, the body comes back re-armed, and the pair alternates forever on life that stays flat (stack 010). Measured at 4.6% on your own draws and 34.3% with this wish. It is lethal but library-bounded — thirty-nine further activations zero a 40-life table, and the library is the hard bound the stack names — so count the whole kill before the first activation.

citations.quote: a tutor is an enabler only if you can cast it and still deploy

targets.scenario: Your board is Yawgmoth, four creatures and a drain. Player 2 is the control seat, has left four or more mana untapped for two turns running, and declined a profitable attack. Assume a sweeper in that hand.
targets.why: Buy the rebuild instead of the restraint, and keep deploying. This wish only works from a to-hand tutor — an instant sitting on top of your library is an instant you do not have when the wrath resolves — which is exactly why it belongs on Demonic. Plumb turns the wave into cards: sacrifice your creatures in response, copy it once per body, draw one more than you sacrificed. With a drain already down, every one of those deaths is damage on the way past.

citations.quote: assume the wrath — over a four-player game one is near-certain — so deploy in waves, hold a rebuild package

targets.scenario: Butcher Ghoul and Geralf's Messenger are on the battlefield with Yawgmoth and Zulaport Cutthroat, a free outlet up, and KILL F is your clock. Three mana spare, and the count says thirty activations against twenty-five cards of margin.
targets.why: Shorten the count nobody else is counting. Stack 014 signed the bare undying pair as library-bounded — lethal at thirty activations, about twenty-five cards to spare — and Pawn banks an Eldrazi Spawn every time a nontoken creature of yours dies. In the cycle that is every single activation: each Spawn refunds {C}, and fed to your outlet it is one more drain trigger per activation, so the same library buys more damage. The Spawn arithmetic is your judgment stacked on a signed bound, not a signed board — say so if you announce it. Seven contained combo records also name Pawn beside Pitiless Plunderer and Reassembling Skeleton; none is signed, so fetch into those as value, never as a stated kill.

citations.quote: Count only hand and board; expected draws are a bonus, not a plan.

tutors.notes: No condition, no delay, no life, no mana-value cap — so fire it at the first genuine hole rather than saving it for a cleverer turn that may not come. It is also the only one of the five to spend on a card costing five or more: what you pay is a turn of board impact, so make the card you name worth a turn.

targets.scenario: Turn five, five mana. Bastion of Remembrance is on the battlefield, Gravecrawler is in your graveyard, and you have three bodies including a token you were going to feed Yawgmoth anyway.
targets.why: Take three cards in one slot: the free repeatable outlet, the Treasure that funds each recast, and the Zombie that lets Gravecrawler cast from the graveyard. Fetch him and stack 009's board is complete — two mana for the wish and three for the body is exactly the five you have, so assemble in one turn. Pay Intent's cost with the token, never a piece; with Bastion out that sacrifice is already a drain trigger, and with Pawn of Ulamog out a nontoken body even refunds a Spawn. KILL A is 1.3% on your own draws and 18.2% with this wish — that jump is the whole reason to spend it here.

citations.quote: Count only hand and board; expected draws are a bonus, not a plan.

targets.scenario: Gravecrawler, Carrion Feeder and Bastion of Remembrance are all on the battlefield. Five mana, Player 3 at 12 with four mana up, and you would rather not hand anyone a turn to find an answer.
targets.why: Take the kill that costs you nothing at all — no life, no cards, no net mana, and your own total climbs while the table falls (stack 011). Carrion Feeder is the Zombie that stays and is never the sacrifice; the Altar's mana ability never uses the stack, so each recast is funded the instant Gravecrawler dies. Pay Intent's own cost with Gravecrawler if you like — he comes straight back for one black. Never pay it with Carrion Feeder.

citations.quote: Prefer win attempts that leave a rebuilt position if they fail

targets.scenario: The wrath resolved. You have one creature left, two cards in hand, five mana, and the table is rebuilding around you. Yawgmoth is castable but there is nothing to feed him.
targets.why: Sacrifice the survivor — it was doing nothing alone — and buy a body every upkeep. Every upkeep, not every turn: in a four-player pod that is up to four deathtouch Snakes a round as long as you keep feeding them to Yawgmoth, and the one you leave standing trades with the biggest thing anyone rebuilds into. Renewable fodder is the class this engine spends fastest, and this is the version that defends while it feeds. Rebuild first and make them react to you.

citations.quote: After the wrath, initiative goes to whoever rebuilds cheapest

targets.scenario: The sweeper took the kill with it. Warren Soultrader and Gravecrawler are both in your graveyard, Bastion of Remembrance survived because it is an enchantment, and you have two small bodies left — a token and a Reassembling Skeleton you rebought. Five mana.
targets.why: Take the wish nobody sees coming, because it turns Intent's cost into the setup. Sacrifice the token to Intent, fetch Victimize, then let Victimize sacrifice the Skeleton and return TWO creature cards tapped — Soultrader and Gravecrawler both, off one card. Tapped costs you nothing here: neither needs to tap and Gravecrawler cannot block anyway. That is a whole kill rebuilt out of the graveyard for five mana, and the Skeleton buys itself back later.

citations.quote: aggressive lines often *create* outs that passive lines close off

tutors.notes: Treat the additional cost as upside almost everywhere: with any drain out it is damage, with Pawn of Ulamog out a nontoken sacrifice refunds a Spawn, with Mikaeus out it is an undying return. It is a genuine tax in exactly three spots — when your only creature is the engine making the others, when you control no creature and the spell is uncastable, and on turn three, where the sim has you at a mean of 1.781 bodies. Read the board before you keep it in an opener.

targets.scenario: Turn four, exactly four mana, a spare token to bargain — a Snake, an Eldrazi Spawn, a Treasure. Yawgmoth lands this turn or is already active, and no engine piece is down.
targets.why: The default fetch, delivered: bargained, Beseech CASTS the card free at mana value 4 or less, and Nest is a 3. Four mana buys the search AND the engine in the same breath — no transit turn, no second cast, and the primary line moves from 7.5% assembled by turn six to 38.9% when a wish backs it. Keep the fuel honest: bargain the token the board replaces by itself, never the drain and never an engine piece.

citations.quote: k tutors plus the card act like k+1 copies of *every* card

targets.scenario: Warren Soultrader and Bastion of Remembrance are already on the battlefield. You have exactly four mana and a spare token, and Player 4 is untapped with two blue sources open, so a counterspell is live and you want the whole line inside one turn.
targets.why: Complete the shape you are already standing in, inside one spell. Mana value 1 sits comfortably under the free-cast cap, and the point is not the mana saved — Beseech exiles the card and casts it, so the loop starts the same turn with nothing else leaving your hand for them to answer. Nothing else fills this slot: Gravecrawler is the single card both unbounded kills route through, and you find him on your own only 17.0% of the time by turn ten.

citations.quote: a named card is 7.1% of your opening seven

targets.scenario: Exquisite Blood resolved two turns ago and the table let it. You have four mana and a spare token to bargain, and the lowest life total at the table is 31.
targets.why: Know your own cap and fetch the half that fits under it. Exquisite Blood is mana value 5 and Beseech can never free-cast it; South Wind Avatar is exactly 4 and sits right on the line, with Marauding Blight-Priest at 3 and Starscape Cleric at 2 if you would rather keep mana up. Stack 012 signed this exact pair — mandatory, not a draw, every opponent to zero at once — so bargain the token, and remember that with a drain out the bargain itself is damage.

citations.quote: wide alpha strikes, loops, commander-damage kills, and each-opponent drains are the payoffs that actually scale

targets.scenario: A Rest in Peace hit the table mid-game and your recursion kills went dark with it. Four mana, a spare token, and your turn.
targets.why: Bargain, search, and cast it free in the same breath — the lock is gone before you pass. Feed the Swarm is mana value 2, well under the cap, and it is the only noncreature answer in the ninety-nine: 17.1% on your own draws, 67.1% with a wish spent on it. The life you pay equals the enchantment's cost; pay it and take your graveyard back. A wish spent on defence is a wish not spent on a kill — spend it anyway, because half your kills live in that graveyard.

citations.quote: ends the game or ends my deck's function

tutors.notes: Two hard edges, both yours to check before you cast. The free cast caps at mana value 4: it reaches Nest of Scarabs, Bastion of Remembrance, Warren Soultrader, Phyrexian Altar, Marauding Blight-Priest, Starscape Cleric, Grave Pact, South Wind Avatar, Feed the Swarm and Jet Medallion, and it never reaches Exquisite Blood or Mikaeus. Never point the free cast at Black Sun's Zenith either — a cast without paying the cost sets X to zero and the wipe is a blank. Bargain fodder is a Treasure, a Snake, a Spawn or a spare token; sacrificing Bastion, Bitterblossom or Nest to find the next piece is the trap this card sets, so pick the fuel before the target. Unbargained it is a four-mana Demonic Tutor to hand — still fine, never the plan.

targets.scenario: Turn eight, six mana. Warren Soultrader and Bastion of Remembrance are on the battlefield, your hand is empty, and Player 3 is the seat most likely to find an answer next turn.
targets.why: Pay the full Spree and take the whole turn with it. The search mode resolves first and puts Gravecrawler on top; the draw mode — pointed at YOURSELF — takes delivery plus two more cards for 3 life. Cast him for one black and stack 009 runs the same turn. Six mana, two extra cards, and no turn handed to the table, where a top-only wish would have made you wait.

citations.quote: its points appreciate as they dwindle, so early points are cheap and late points are priceless

targets.scenario: Mid-game grind. Yawgmoth has been answered once, so the next trip costs six, your hand holds three black spells, and you have three mana spare at sorcery speed.
targets.why: Book the rebate. Three mana puts the Medallion on top, you draw and cast it for two, and every black spell for the rest of the game costs one less — the commander's taxed recast drops to five and the hand you are holding ships a turn earlier. Fast mana is the thinnest engine class on the sheet at 43.6%, and Dark Ritual's window closed on turn one; a standing cost cut is the acceleration a wish can still buy in the mid-game. Judgment, stated as such: the goldfish models no cost reducers, so this value never appears in a number.

citations.quote: coming out too slowly is an easy way to lose a game

targets.scenario: Yawgmoth has been answered twice — the next trip from the zone costs eight. Your board holds Bitterblossom, Ayara and two drains, so your devotion to black is six. Three mana spare at sorcery speed.
targets.why: The odd one nobody sees coming: a wish on a land. Book Nykthos, draw it, and it is your land drop — no cast, no window for anyone to answer — then two mana and a tap pay six black off that board, which is most of the recast from one land. Know what the sheet says and why: the colour-source count gives Nykthos no unconditional credit because its mana is conditional, and that is the count being conservative, not the land being bad. Your board is the credit — seventy-six black pips across fifty-five spells means devotion assembles itself here. Fetch it at devotion four or better; below that you have booked a colorless land.

citations.quote: each return trip to the command zone adds {2} per prior command-zone cast

targets.scenario: Endgame. Player 3 is at 3 after paying for their own fetches and a Necropotence of their own, the other two seats are in the high teens, and you have five mana and a board of black permanents.
targets.why: Nobody counts this one, so count it: cast the full Spree, let the search book Gray Merchant, and point the draw mode at PLAYER 3 — who draws three cards, loses 3 life, and is gone before the cards matter. Then the Merchant lands next turn for devotion in a list carrying seventy-six black pips across fifty-five spells. One seat removed by the tutor itself, the rest drained by what it fetched. Expect the coalition to form that turn and have your next two turns planned before you cast it.

citations.quote: time them for the turn they win, not the turn they impress

tutors.notes: Read it as two tutors and pick which one you are casting. At three mana it is a slower Demonic that lands on top and costs a turn — fine when you have a turn to spend, and the only sensible delivery for a land. At five it is the only card in the deck that fetches and delivers in one breath, and 3 life is the right price in a shell that gains one back per drain trigger. The mode order is in your favour: the search resolves before the draw, so pointing the draw at yourself always takes delivery of what you just booked.

gaps: No wish finds an artifact answer, because none exists to find — enumerated over all eighty entries, nothing in the ninety-nine destroys or exiles an opposing artifact. Feed the Swarm covers creature and enchantment; Bojuka Bog is one graveyard exile riding on a land. Against a resolved Cursed Totem or Grafdigger's Cage your outs are speed, politics and somebody else's removal — buy that removal with your own spot answers and your silence, and overpay. These five cards make you faster; they cannot make you broader.

No search finds your commander, because all five say search your library and Yawgmoth sits in the command zone. Buy the insurance before the removal, not after: Lightning Greaves ahead of the targeting, Supernatural Stamina or Malakir Rebirth in response, and Phyrexian Reclamation, Animate Dead or Victimize once he is in the graveyard.

There is no union kill rate and you must never quote one. The goldfish prices each shape independently, so a hand holding Exquisite Blood, Gravecrawler and Zulaport Cutthroat satisfies three groups while assembling nothing. Quote 42.6%, 34.3%, 26.9%, 18.2% and 12.0% separately, and quote the engine's 38.9%-by-turn-six on its own.

The assisted figures model ONE wish: the sim fills a single missing group with a single drawn, affordable tutor, and a top-of-library tutor costs a turn. Read them as floors when you hold two tutors and ceilings when you hold none, and plan the turn accordingly.

Nest of Scarabs is one card deep and the primary line runs through it — a named card is about 7% of an opening seven, and these five tutors are its only redundancy. You draw one of them in 61.2% of games by turn ten; below that number the fetch does not exist, so keep a fair drain-and-grind plan running underneath every engine plan.

Nykthos never shows its value on the source sheet: restriction-aware counting gives a conditional land no unconditional colour credit, and that call stands. Judge it on the battlefield instead — count your devotion before you book it, and treat any wish on it below devotion four as a mistake the sheet correctly priced at zero.

The containment records name far more lines than the checker has signed: thirty-nine combo lines sit fully inside this list, eleven of them two-card infinites, against fourteen signed boards. The Yawgmoth + Pawn of Ulamog + Zulaport Cutthroat + Butcher Ghoul record even claims infinite draw — it needs a stack scenario before anyone announces it. Fetch into unsigned lines as value when the board asks; never narrate them as kills.

Nothing here prices a tutor against a resolved tax effect — the goldfish models no opponents. Under a Sphere or a Thalia, keep the one- and two-mana tutors live, remember Jet Medallion rebates a mana on every black spell, and lean on your commander's ability, which costs no mana at all and is your best card by a wider margin than any of these five.
